text:
maya: heads up, saw a ~200ms tail latency spike on canary at 03:40 UTC tied to kv paging under sustained long-context load

sam: ugh, more evict noise. any repro steps?

maya: repro is pretty consistent — run long-context streaming workload (avg seq 8k, 75th 12k) with batching heuristics enabled and kernel auto-swap on. after ~10m memory slowly grows then a burst of paging + evictions -> tail.

li: do you have flamegraphs or allocation samples?

maya: attaching trimmed profiler snippet: 
```
CPU: kv-evicter loop woke 1.2k times / sec
KV misses rose from 3% -> 18% before spike
Pager IO spikes ~4x concurrent with a kernel transition log: 
[2026-03-05T03:40:21Z] kernel_select: switched->quant_fast (seq dist changed)
[2026-03-05T03:40:22Z] batcher: increased target_batch=64 -> 128
```

oliver: interesting that kernel swap and batch increase line up. might be that larger batches change hotset locality and evicter LRU ordering flips to FIFO-ish due to reinserts.

sam: fifo vs lru question: is our evict policy deterministic across concurrent reinsert + paging? we had races before where reinsert puts item at tail and pager removes older entries incorrectly.

li: looked at logs, saw patterns like: 
```
EVICT start id=0x7fb page=123 slot=54 policy=LRU
REINSERT id=0x7fb slot=10 -> move_to_front
PAGEOUT slot=54 -> freed
```
which is fine but when batcher amplifies concurrency we see reorder: REINSERT happens after EVICT decision but before actual removal -> ghost entries and reuse misses.

maya: bottom line: correctness looks intact (no corruption), but ordering + timing under bigger batches causes reuse window to shrink -> more paging and higher tail latency.

oliver: is this specific to quant_fast kernel? maybe its KV layout changes or per-thread cache alignment leads to fragmentation.

li: quick hypothesis list: 
- batch size increase increases parallelism and contention on slab arenas -> fragmentation.
- kernel swap changes per-request memory footprint -> hotspot remapping.
- evicter current handshake assumes synchronous remove but we run async pager which creates reorder window.

sam: we should produce a minimal repro that flips just one variable at a time (batcher on/off, kernel fixed, async pager sync). can we run small-scale test?

maya: running now: 3 runs — baseline (batch=64, kernel pinned), batch=128 pinned, batch=128 kernel auto-swap. will post logs.

perf-bot: Automated perf alert: canary throughput nominal; tail latency regression +38% at 2026-03-05T03:40:21Z. Trace: https://perf/redwood/trace/5189012345

oliver: thanks. if repro holds, I want to try a quick fix: add a brief per-slot CAS during evict to ensure reinsert after decision fails (recheck) — basically make eviction conditional on current slot owner id. cheap && helps ordering.

li: that will add cost to evict path though. alternative: delay async pager flush by a micro-window to let in-flight reinserts finish. or make reinserts bump a generation counter so evict checks gen mismatch.

sam: can we measure the cost? add a bench: evict-rate * cas-cost. evict-rate ~ 1.2k/s so overhead probably small.

maya: test results (summary):
- baseline pinned: no spike, stable memory
- batch=128 pinned: small mem jitter but no paging spike
- batch=128 auto-swap: reproduced 3/3 -> paging + 150-220ms tail

oliver: that points to kernel swap interplay. maybe the kernel selects quant_fast which uses slightly different KV chunk sizes causing atomization of entries and more reinsert churn.

li: proposed immediate mitigations: 
1) short-term: pin kernel selection for canary workloads until we mitigate ordering (env flag)
2) medium: add CAS check in evict path (opt-in via runtime flag), bench first
3) long-term: redesign evict handshake to use per-entry versioning (cheap reads) so reinsert/evict races are provably ordered

sam: agree. also add a telemetry gauge: reinsert-after-evict counts and slot-gen mismatches so we can quantify.

maya: I'll flip pin for canary and run perf-run. li, oliver: can you prototype CAS change in a branch? keep it behind flag.

oliver: on it. I'll add microbench and a simple correctness assert that fails loudly in test mode.

li: I'll instrument telemetry and add a lightweight gen counter in-memory only for now.

sam: cross-check with rollout policy — if we pin kernel we need to add note in console that canary is pinned (ops awareness).

maya: thanks everyone. CC-ing perf-bot added traces. will update with run ids: run-6421 (pinned), run-6422 (batch128 pinned), run-6423 (batch128 auto).

perf-bot: Trace snapshots: run-6422: https://perf/redwood/snap/6422, run-6423: https://perf/redwood/snap/6423

oliver: plan: next 48h -> branch with CAS + bench, telemetry + dashboard tile, pin kernel on canary. 48-72h -> decision on gen-based refactor.

maya: sounds good. leaving action items in thread:
- maya: pin canary kernel + rerun (done)
- li: telemetry gen counter + tile (in progress)
- oliver: evict CAS PR behind flag + bench (in progress)
- sam: add ops note in console and watch release (todo)

sam: tiny note — ensure we test with mixed clients (chat + embeddings) since workload mix affects hotset.

maya: yep included. will report back tomorrow with perf numbers. :thumbsup:
